clue.text: Forest close to Parkhurst is burning

parts.note: the Forest of Arden, the woodland of As You Like It

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: Something is on fire in the woods near Parkhurst prison on the Isle of Wight.
explanation.walkthrough: Parkhurst is a prison on the Isle of Wight; its closing letter T follows ARDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent is literally fiery and glowing, a synonym of burning, as well as passionate.

clue.text: A vessel reportedly held in place

indicators.note: reportedly means the phrase is said aloud and the entry matches its sound

parts.note: a tanker is a vessel carrying oil or other liquid

explanation.surface: A ship is said to have been detained.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, A TANKER sounds like the two-word answer, a moored ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that is moored by its anchor is held fixed in one place.

clue.text: Decide to discourage store

parts.note: to deter is to discourage
a mine is a store or rich supply, as in a mine of information

explanation.surface: Someone chooses to put others off a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine is to settle or resolve, a synonym of decide.

clue.text: River running out of salmon, I learned

indicators.note: the answer runs out of the words, its letters lying inside them in sequence

explanation.surface: An angler discovers a river has no more salmon left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running out of' looks like a lack of fish, but signals letters taken from salmoN I LEarned.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great African river flowing north through Egypt.

clue.text: Writ large, a page inside Guardian?

indicators.note: inside means the page letter goes within the phrase a guardian

parts.note: a parent is a child's guardian

explanation.surface: A reader wonders whether a story is splashed across a page of the Guardian newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian looks like the British newspaper, but it is a guardian, a parent; P goes inside A PARENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something writ large is plainly visible, which is what obvious or evident means.

clue.text: Day trip abroad, a profitable success

indicators.note: abroad suggests the letters being sent wandering out of their places

explanation.surface: A holiday excursion overseas turns out to be a money-spinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitting pay dirt originally meant striking gold-bearing earth, so it means a lucrative discovery.

clue.text: Native with blood group not seen before

parts.note: AB is one of the human blood groups
something original is new, never seen before

explanation.surface: A local person has a rare blood type nobody has encountered before.
explanation.definitionFit: An aboriginal inhabitant is one present from the earliest times, a native.

clue.text: No ball, perhaps, in over

definitions.meaning: in cricket a no ball is one kind of run conceded beyond the batsman's score
over in the sense of additional, surplus to what is needed

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire calls an illegal delivery during an over.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls; a no ball, wide or bye scores a run to the batting side not off the bat, and is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: A no ball gives the batting side a bonus run of that name, and the word also means surplus or additional.

clue.text: Hat, good sort

definitions.meaning: a tall silk hat worn with formal dress
old-fashioned slang for a decent, likeable person

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a top hat, and dated British slang for a fine fellow.

clue.text: Awfully remote shooting star

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are badly treated and knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A falling star seen terribly far away.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting star is the popular name for a meteor burning up in the sky.

clue.text: Powerful guns, hostile positioned in main road

indicators.note: positioned in means one piece is placed within another

parts.note: an artery is a main road or major route
ill can mean unfriendly or hostile, as in ill will

explanation.surface: Heavy weapons have been stationed by an enemy along a highway.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery is the collective term for large mounted guns used in warfare.

clue.text: Readily available over in Antwerp at noon

indicators.note: over means the found letters are turned over, read backwards
in means the letters sit within the run of words Antwerp at noon

explanation.surface: Something can be easily had in a Belgian city at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside antwerP AT NOon sits PATNO, which 'over' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer on tap is drawn from a cask at once, so the phrase means ready for use.

clue.text: Short cut round centre of Derby

indicators.note: round means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter

explanation.surface: A quick route avoids the middle of the English city of Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short cut' reads as a phrase, but 'Short' is the definition and 'cut' goes round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A curt reply is brief to the point of rudeness, so short.

clue.text: Run away with one friend to find fair

parts.note: leg it is British slang for run off
I is the Roman numeral for one
mate is British slang for a friend

explanation.surface: Someone elopes with a companion to reach a funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leg it' is informal British English for running away.
explanation.definitionFit: Legitimate means lawful and justifiable, so fair in the sense of allowable.

clue.text: Instrument, German one, party introduced to pop singer

indicators.note: introduced to means the pieces are put into the singer's name

parts.note: Dido is a British pop singer known by that single name
I is the Roman numeral for one
a do is informal for a party

explanation.surface: A German brings an instrument to a party for a pop star.
explanation.walkthrough: Dido, the British pop star, is split open to take the German, one and party pieces before her final O.
explanation.definitionFit: The didgeridoo is a long wooden wind instrument of the Australian Aboriginal peoples.

clue.text: Shakespearean actor, one appearing in musical!

indicators.note: appearing in means one piece shows up inside another

parts.note: Oliver! is the Lionel Bart musical based on Oliver Twist
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A classical stage actor turns up in a song-and-dance show.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark nods to the musical's title, Oliver!
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was the great English stage and screen actor famed for his Shakespeare roles.

clue.text: First in box in court case concerning an ethnic group

indicators.note: in here means the letter is placed within the court case

parts.note: a trial is a court case

indicators.note: the first in a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: The first item in evidence at a lawsuit about a minority community.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal describes something relating to a tribe, a social or ethnic grouping.

clue.text: Putting down in a cellar

parts.note: a basement is a cellar, the storey below ground

explanation.surface: Something is being stored below ground level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting down' looks like laying something in storage, but means humiliating.
explanation.definitionFit: Abasement is humiliation, the act of lowering someone in esteem, so putting down.

clue.text: Small amount of cash deposited in bank not long ago

indicators.note: deposited in means one piece is put into another

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: A little money was paid into the bank lately.
explanation.definitionFit: Recently means lately, at a time not long past.

clue.text: British bird dog

parts.note: an eagle is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A British bird of prey and a hound.
explanation.definitionFit: The beagle is a small hound breed used for hunting hares.

clue.text: Advocate has degree in English Language

indicators.note: in means one piece sits within the others

parts.note: Norse is the old Scandinavian language

explanation.surface: A lawyer holds a qualification in English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advocate' looks like a noun for a barrister, but is the verb, to support.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse something is to back it publicly, which is to advocate it.

clue.text: Traditional beer — all are drunk before end of wake

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are tipsy and staggering out of order
the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Mourners down plenty of old-style ale before a funeral gathering finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: A wake is a gathering after a funeral; 'drunk' scrambles the letters of 'all are', and 'end of wake' adds the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Real ale is the British term for cask-conditioned beer brewed in the traditional way.

clue.text: Fancy gold being rejected by Chanel

indicators.note: being rejected means the word is sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
Coco Chanel was the French fashion designer

explanation.surface: Elaborate gold jewellery is turned down by a French fashion house.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is the ornate eighteenth-century style, hence elaborately decorated or fancy.

clue.text: Bishop leaving one English town for another

indicators.note: leaving means the letter departs from the town's name

parts.note: Beccles is a market town in Suffolk
B is the abbreviation for bishop in chess notation

explanation.surface: A churchman moves from one town in England to a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: Beccles is in Suffolk; dropping its B gives a town near Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccles is a town in Greater Manchester, so another English town.

clue.text: Argue against policeman breaking agreement

indicators.note: breaking means the agreement is broken open and a piece put inside

parts.note: a contract is a binding agreement
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: Someone disputes the claim that an officer violated a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To contradict someone is to deny what they say, so to argue against them.

clue.text: Statesman from Croxton or Thetford

indicators.note: from means the answer is drawn out of the run of words

explanation.surface: A politician hails from one of two Norfolk places.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is croxtoN OR THetford; Lord North was British prime minister during the American Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord North was the eighteenth-century British prime minister, a statesman.

clue.text: Nothing more than a pond

definitions.meaning: only, just, as in a trifling amount
a lake or pool of water

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective meaning only and a poetic noun for a small lake.

clue.text: The answer to this one must be written down!

definitions.text: The answer to this one must be written down!

parts.words: The answer to this one must be written down!
parts.note: every crossword hint has its solution written into the grid, and this is a down entry

explanation.definitionFit: A crossword clue's answer is written into the grid, and this one runs down.

clue.text: Sensational cover with ancient city featured inside

indicators.note: featured inside means the city is placed within the cover

parts.note: a lid is a cover
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A tabloid front page shows a lost civilisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid means shockingly vivid, as in sensationalist press stories.

clue.text: Look back on extremely remarkable harvest

indicators.note: extremely means the extremes, the outer letters, of the next word

parts.note: to harvest is to collect or gather

explanation.surface: A farmer recalls an exceptional crop.
explanation.definitionFit: To recollect is to remember, to cast the mind back over something.

clue.text: Vessel more willingly boarded by companion

indicators.note: boarded by means the companion gets on board, inside the other piece

parts.note: sooner means rather, more willingly
CH is Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A ship that a shipmate would rather climb aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Companion of Honour is a British order, abbreviated CH; it boards the ship just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a sailing ship with two or more masts, a vessel.

clue.text: Watch son coming on to stage

parts.note: an actor's entry is coming onstage

explanation.surface: A parent sees their boy walk on in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: a guard.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is a guard on duty, and a sentry is a soldier posted on watch.
